name: Cleveland Yutaka Corporation
old_description: Cleveland Yutaka Corporation is a precision machining manufacturer of the automotive industry and a subsidiary of Yutaka Industry Co., LTD.
about:
Cleveland Yutaka Corporation operates in Shelby, North Carolina, as a subsidiary of Japan's Yutaka Industry Co., Ltd. The company was incorporated in June 1995 and completed its initial 56,788-square-foot facility in February 1996, launching production with 20 employees. A 2015 expansion added 52,552 square feet, bringing the plant to 109,340 square feet.

The shop specializes in high-volume, high-precision machined components using CNC machining, centerless grinding, and centered grinding. It holds diameter tolerances to 0.008 mm (8 µm) and surface finishes to 3.2 Rz, with standard capability targets above 3σ and special-characteristic targets above 4σ. Materials processed include aluminum, hardened and non-hardened steel, stainless steel, and cast iron. In-line and off-line visual and dimensional inspection, backed by proprietary and outsourced equipment, enables 100% nonconformity detection.

CYC serves the automotive sector, supplying components for fuel pumps, blower fans, starters, alternators, power-window drive shafts, solenoids, and suspension systems. Its customer base includes Toyota, Ford, General Motors, Chrysler, Hyundai, Honda, and other major OEMs.

The company states its goals as zero failed deliveries, zero late deliveries, and 100% quality. It emphasizes continuous improvement, employee development, and environmental responsibility through waste reduction, regulatory compliance, and safe chemical management.

name: Coastal Automotive
old_description: Coastal Automotive leverages innovation, precision, industry-leading resources and rapid development and production capabilities to transform your energy management challenges into solutions.
about:
Coastal Automotive, headquartered in Holland, Michigan, was founded in 2007 as a manufacturer of passive energy management solutions for the mobility sector. The company operates additional manufacturing facilities in Rochester Hills, Michigan, and maintains sales and engineering offices in Seoul and Tokyo. Ownership details are not publicly disclosed.

The company produces energy-absorbing components using proprietary foam materials—IMPAXX™ and TereSorb™—through processes that include die cutting, vacuum and cold forming, compression molding, CNC wire cutting, and 3D printing for customized parts. It offers CAE services, product development, and assembly, with a stated capability to move from prototype to high-volume production without traditional tooling.

Coastal Automotive serves automotive OEMs, motorsports (including NASCAR, for which it is the energy management provider), heavy-truck, marine, and aftermarket customers. Its Michigan headquarters sits near the North American operations of a dozen OEMs, and its global offices support customers across time zones.

The company emphasizes sustainability, recycling 100 percent of unused foam scrap into polystyrene-based products and crafting TereSorb from 100 percent recycled bottles. It operates under Six Sigma and Lean disciplines, holds ISO 9001 and IATF 16949 certifications, and has earned multiple GM Supplier of the Year awards.

name: Coastal Electronics, LLC
old_description: is a woman-owned small business located in Westerly, Rhode Island. We named our company in honor of the beautiful ocean scenery surrounding our area.
about:
Coastal Electronics, LLC is a woman-owned small business based in Westerly, Rhode Island. The company took its name from the ocean scenery that surrounds the area.

The firm operates as a distributor and supply-chain service provider, specializing in electronic components, fasteners, cabling, connectors, and sockets. It purchases directly from manufacturers such as Mill-Max, GE Fanuc, Samtec, and Amontec, and maintains access to surplus inventory from OEMs and contract electronics manufacturers. Services include piece-count quality control, counterfeit-part guarantees, third-party testing and certification, surplus-inventory advertising and physical inventory, immediate RFQ response, stocking programs with blanket-order support, and consolidated billing and shipping with sub-packaging for clear identification.

Customers include original equipment manufacturers, contract electronics manufacturers, and government contractors seeking hard-to-find parts or proposal pricing. The company also sources non-electronic items such as furniture, racking, paints, and chemicals, drop-shipped directly from manufacturers.

Coastal Electronics emphasizes a hands-on approach: every part is piece-counted rather than weighed, counterfeit parts are guaranteed against, and the team works directly with buyers and engineers to develop quotes for government bids. Consolidated invoicing and coordinated receiving support are offered to reduce administrative burden.

name: Coherent
old_description: See why the rapid growth in AI/ML is driving a demand for faster datacom enabled by innovative Coherent solutions.
about:
Coherent is headquartered in Starkville, Mississippi. The company was founded in 1971 and has grown into a global photonics enterprise operating in more than 20 countries.

Coherent designs and manufactures lasers, optical components, and photonic systems for datacenter, communications, and industrial markets. Its product portfolio includes optical transceivers, active optical cables, silicon photonics devices, VCSEL arrays, and laser systems for precision manufacturing, semiconductor processing, and display fabrication. The company also supplies capital equipment for semiconductor and display production, such as excimer laser annealing and laser lift-off systems, and has announced the modernization and expansion of its Sherman facility with support from a proposed $50 million CHIPS Act award.

Customers span hyperscale datacenter operators, telecommunications network providers, automotive and energy manufacturers, semiconductor and display fabs, and research and medical institutions. Coherent's industrial lasers serve metal and plastic cutting, welding, marking, and ablation applications, while its instrumentation products support scientific research, OEM integration, and clinical settings. The company also provides photonic components for fusion energy research.

Coherent emphasizes its vertically integrated supply chain for datacom transceivers, combining silicon photonics, VCSELs, lenses, filters, and isolators to reduce supply chain uncertainty. The company cites its broad technology stack, global scale, and ISO-certified quality management as key differentiators, and has formed a strategic partnership with NVIDIA to develop optics technology for next-generation data center architecture.
